item.title: Five New Democrat State Trifectas: Assisted Suicide, Here We Come

item.content:encoded:
The national elections, just completed, added five states that will be completely controlled by Democrats next year, i.e., legislature and governor. They are, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin.

Every one of these is ripe for , as that policy is now part of the liberal/progressive issue agenda. Most have already seen serious efforts to legalize doctor-prescribed death — even when Republicans held some power. Indeed, the electorally late (defeated for reelection) Governor Joe Lombardo of Nevada vetoed a legalization bill a few years ago.

Other states that are already governed by a so-called Democratic trifecta, but which have not yet legalized assisted suicide, are Virginia, Maryland, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island. Efforts have been made to legalize assisted suicide in all of these as well, with Massachusetts voters rejecting assisted suicide in 2012 — thanks in large part to the opposition by Ted Kennedy’s widow.

I think all of these states will see renewed legalization attempts in the next two years. At least a few will pass. That’s not a sure thing, of course. Indeed, last year I was pleasantly surprised when Virginia Democrats defeated a bill in committee. But Governor Spanberger supports legalization, so I am sure they will try again.

The primary hope of preventing legalization in blue trifecta states rests with the , which is part of the liberal/progressive coalition, but sees — correctly, in my view — assisted suicide as targeting them. Civil rights activists, legislators of color, and more traditional Democrats also often oppose assisted suicide. Pro-lifers and medical associations have a part to play, too. It takes a strange bedfellow coalition to defeat these bills in Democrat-controlled states, so we’ll see how it goes.

The other Democratic trifecta states have already legalized assisted suicide. But that is never the end of it. The first laws passed are not meant to be ceilings but launching pads. So, expect bills in at least some of these states to be filed loosening eligibility or otherwise allowing more sick people to get dead faster.

Because there can never be enough assisted suicide.

An editorial in (once again) extols redefining climate change as a health issue to allow technocrats to exert greater control over policy — and along the way even extols as an exemplar of the cause. From “Climate Change and Health: 10 Years On, What’s Next?”

Despite their efforts, the editorial grouses, things are only getting worse. Blame the usual suspects!

item.content:encoded:
Once again, well-meaning advocates are pushing kidney-selling as a means to shorten the organ transplant waiting list.

The push is on to pass the (HR 2687) before the end of the current Congress. The bill would start a pilot program in which the government would buy kidneys from living people — through a $50,000 total ($10,000 per year) tax credit — if they’re “donating” (selling) to a stranger.
